title: Frontend entry domain css box model
topic: Frontend entry domain css box model
question: What is the CSS box model, and how does the box-sizing property change how width and height are calculated?
idealAnswer:
Every element is a box made of four layers, from inside out: content, padding, border, and margin

By default (content-box), width and height apply only to the content area, so padding and border are added on top, making the rendered box larger than the specified width

box-sizing: border-box changes width and height to include padding and border, so the specified size is the final rendered size, which is usually easier to reason about in layouts

Margin is always outside the box and is not included in either box-sizing mode, and adjacent vertical margins can collapse into a single margin

Many teams set a global border-box reset (e.g. on the universal selector) specifically to avoid the surprise of padding/border expanding an element beyond its intended width
